content: 1. Elagolix increases the level or effect of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, it decreases the level or effect of budesonide by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, so co-administration with CYP3A substrates may require dose adjustments. Monitor closely. 2. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of eletriptan by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Eliglustat increases budesonide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapeutic drug concentrations should be monitored, and dosage adjustments of P-gp substrates may be necessary. Monitor closely. 4. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and is contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have a high risk of serious or life-threatening events due to elevated plasma concentrations. Monitor closely. 5. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Monitor closely. 6. Budesonide may decrease the anticoagulant effects of enoxaparin by increasing blood coagulability, but it may also impair vascular integrity, increasing bleeding risk. Monitor INR closely. 7. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of eplerenone by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of ergotamine by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of erlotinib by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin base increases budesonide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide decreases erythromycin levels by enhancing its CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases budesonide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide decreases erythromycin levels by enhancing its CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Erythromycin lactobionate increases budesonide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide decreases erythromycin levels by enhancing its CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Erythromycin stearate increases budesonide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide decreases erythromycin levels by enhancing its CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases budesonide levels by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Esomeprazole decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely and consider modifying therapy. 16. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of estradiol by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of conjugated synthetic estrogens by enhancing their hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of estropipate by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Budesonide and ethacrynic acid may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypokalemia, especially with strong glucocorticoid activity. Monitor closely. 20. Budesonide and etodolac may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of etravirine by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Etravirine also decreases budesonide levels through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of eucalyptus by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of everolimus by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Famotidine decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely and consider modifying therapy. 25. Fedratinib increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Monitor closely. 26. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of felodipine by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Felodipine increases budesonide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Budesonide and fenoprofen may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of fesoterodine by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Budesonide decreases the effects of feverfew through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 30. Fexinidazole increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 31. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of finasteride by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 32. Budesonide increases the effects of fingolimod through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Concomitant therapy may enhance immunosuppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Fluconazole increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of fludrocortisone by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Budesonide and fluoxymesterone may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing edema formation. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 36. Budesonide and flurbiprofen may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Fluvoxamine increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Budesonide may decrease the anticoagulant effects of fondaparinux by increasing blood coagulability, but it may also impair vascular integrity, increasing bleeding risk. Monitor INR closely. 39. Fosamprenavir increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide decreases fosamprenavir levels by enhancing its CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Fosaprepitant increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide decreases fosaprepitant levels by enhancing its CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Fosphenytoin decreases budesonide levels by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Budesonide and furosemide may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypokalemia, especially with strong glucocorticoid activity. Monitor closely. 43. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases budesonide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Budesonide decreases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 45. Grapefruit increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Griseofulvin decreases budesonide levels by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Budesonide decreases the effects of the Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid vaccination during chemotherapy or radiation therapy if possible, as antibody response may be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy discontinuation if immune competence is restored. Monitor closely. 48. Budesonide may decrease the anticoagulant effects of heparin by increasing blood coagulability, but it may also impair vascular integrity, increasing bleeding risk. Monitor INR closely. 49. Budesonide decreases the effects of the hepatitis A vaccine (inactivated) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Budesonide decreases the effects of the hepatitis A/B vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 51. Budesonide decreases the effects of the hepatitis A/typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 52. Budesonide decreases the effects of the hepatitis B vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Corticosteroids also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. This combination is contraindicated. 53. Budesonide decreases the effects of the human papillomavirus vaccine (nonavalent) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Immunosuppressive therapies, including corticosteroids, may reduce immune responses to vaccines. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Budesonide and hydrochlorothiazide may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypokalemia, especially with strong glucocorticoid activity. Monitor closely. 55. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of hydrocortisone by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Budesonide decreases the level or effect of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by enhancing its hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Budesonide and ibuprofen may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor closely and consider modifying therapy. 59. Idelalisib increases budesonide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Corticosteroids may be needed to treat severe diarrhea or colitis associated with idelalisib therapy. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are known to increase systemic exposure to oral budesonide. Use caution and monitor closely.
